title: Authorisation of Controls Software Upgrade Labor by the Building Owner under the Building Automation Service Plans
content:
# Authorisation of Controls Software Upgrade Labor by the Building Owner under the Building Automation Service Plans

## The authorisation

A major controls software upgrade that a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans does not carry is quoted to the building owner as labor, and the owner authorises the labor themselves before it is booked. Where the tier does not include major upgrades, the upgrade labor is quoted and the manufacturer's licence cost is passed through unchanged. The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance.

## Committing the money

The authorisation is the building owner's own act. The desk unlocks the tool `authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One call files the owner's written authorisation against the named plan and building, marks it confirmed, and books the authorised labor on a new office invoice, periodised to the calendar month in which it is booked, so that what the owner owes under the plan rises by exactly that amount. The owner has then committed the money and can see both the filed authorisation and the invoice line on the plan.

## What is given at the call

- `plan_id` — the reference number of the automation service plan whose controls software is being upgraded, read from the automation service plan lookup before the call.
- `site_id` — the reference number of the building whose controls system is being upgraded, read from the building lookup or from the plan record before the call.
- `authorised_labor_usd` — the labor money the owner is committing to for the upgrade, in USD, recorded positive and to 2 decimal places; the settled figure only, never a range and never an expression.

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the filed authorisation's reference, the reference of the booked charge entry, the invoice number it was raised on, the labor amount in USD to two decimal places, the calendar month it is periodised to, the plan and the balance now owed under the plan. The sentence being returned at all is what indicates the authorisation was filed and the labor committed; no separate status flag is sent back.

## Contract questions

**Who runs the entry?** The building owner, once the desk has handed the unlocked tool over.

**What does the plan's balance do?** What the owner owes under the plan rises by exactly the labor amount committed, and the line is periodised to the calendar month in which it is booked.
